turns.content: Hi, I'm the AIowa Service Guide, an AI assistant. What would you like help with?

Hi, I run Copper Mesa Supply, a plumbing supply business. Uh, 6 staff handle quote requests arriving by email. They copy details into Excel, but some requests are getting missed. Uh, we want help collecting details and um, you know, it's it's got to be uh, pretty spot on without errors and uh, how could you guys help with that?

I can help with that. Let me check what AIowa Agents can do for this kind of workflow.

AIowa Agents can help with that kind of workflow. It designs and builds AI agents for small businesses that handle inbox triage — reading, sorting, and flagging incoming emails — and can chase quotes and requests that might otherwise get missed. The agent works inside the tools you already use, like your inbox, and everything starts in draft mode with human approval built in.

So for your quote requests, the agent could read each incoming email, pull out the details, and flag or route them so nothing slips through. You'd set the approval level — for example, whether it just drafts the details for your team to review, or does more.

I can't confirm whether it would be "spot on without errors" in the way you're hoping — that depends on the specifics of your emails and setup, and I don't have approved information guaranteeing error-free extraction. What I can say is that the documented workflow is built around human approval, so your team would have a checkpoint.

One question that would help me point you in the right direction: when you say "collecting details," do you mean pulling the quote info out of the email into your Excel sheet, or more about making sure every request gets noticed and followed up on?

Got it — both pulling the details into your sheet and making sure every request gets noticed.

For the extraction side, the documented workflow is built around your existing tools, so the agent would work with your inbox and your Excel setup rather than adding a new dashboard. It starts in draft mode, meaning the details it pulls would come to your team for review before anything is finalized. That's the human-approval checkpoint I mentioned.

I should be clear about the "spot on without errors" part: I don't have approved information that guarantees error-free extraction. The documented safeguard is the approval level you choose — you can set it so your team reviews the details before they're used. Whether that meets your accuracy bar would depend on the specifics of your quote emails, and I can't confirm that fit from here.

For the missed-requests side, the agent can read, sort, and flag every inbound email, and it can chase quotes and requests that might otherwise die in the inbox — timed, polite follow-ups based on your approval settings.

So the two pieces map to: (1) a draft-mode extraction workflow into your existing tools, and (2) inbox triage plus follow-up so nothing gets overlooked.

Would it be useful if I prepared a short note for a human to review, capturing what you've described — the missed quote requests, the Excel workflow, and your accuracy requirement — so someone can look at the specifics?
Yeah, please prepare that information for a human review. Don't send anything yet. And and um, one correction, uh, go go ahead and do that. get that ready for human review.
I've prepared the local human-review note with the details you provided.
Great. Hey, one correction, 4 staff handle those requests, not 6. Uh, we also use a supplier portal, but I don't know whether it has an API.
